content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm new to [product_name] but have experience programming with other PLC brands. My goal is to route a 4-20mA signal from an input channel to an output channel, but during a specific operation (like cleaning the pressure sensor on the analog input), I need the output to remain unchanged so the system doesn't trigger alarms. Cleaning causes the sensor to spike and would otherwise lead to unnecessary alerts. Has anyone implemented this before? I already have timers and digital outputs set up for the cleaning process; both function block and ladder work, but is function block better for analog? Thanks!
This is a basic example of how to stop the analog output signal.
You can use either FBD or LAD programming; both options work. See the attachment for a concise solution. Regards, [user_name]
Thank you all! This is exactly what I needed.

analysis.insight_summary: Users discussed a simple approach for freezing an analog output signal during system maintenance, using [product_name] PLCs. The original poster is new to this product but experienced in automation, seeking to prevent alarms while a pressure sensor is cleaned. Community replies confirm that both Function Block Diagram and Ladder Diagram programming are suitable, and members quickly shared effective solutions, showing the product’s flexibility for this scenario.
